PullRequest.Title: agentHost: grant automation customization access
PullRequest.Body:
## Motivation

Automations can persist client-served customizations so remote Agent Hosts can capture them for scheduled runs. Create and update actions did not grant read access before dispatch, causing remote hosts to reject valid saves. This PR applies the same narrow implicit-read grants already used by active session customizations.

## Changes made

- Grant read access for customizations attached to automation create and update actions.
- Add regression coverage for both automation action paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create an automation with client-served customizations on a local or remote Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The store resolves its customization scope, dispatches the create action, and waits for authoritative catalog state. The added URI iteration registers grants synchronously but does not await realpath before dispatch. Host capture, persistence, and response remain on the save critical path; subsequent permission checks can await grant realpath promises.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the canonical path for each newly registered customization grant through the file provider, potentially crossing provider IPC/network boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most U provider realpath operations per connection's first encounter with these URIs; zero additional grant realpath calls for already granted URIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automation create did not register these grants; a URI previously granted by an active session already had the same realpath work and is deduplicated after this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started before dispatch but not awaited there; remote resource permission checks may subsequently await the stored promises.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one dispatch notification, then use existing reverse resourceResolve/resourceList/resourceRead requests to copy uncached client bundles; encode/decode resource bytes as base64.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action notification; metadata/list requests scale with traversed bundle entries and content reads with uncached files/bytes. Local file customizations used in place avoid remote copies; cached destinations skip copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same capture and transport path existed. Reads could already succeed with existing grants; otherwise the operation was denied. This change authorizes intended reads rather than adding a second copy, changing serialization, or increasing per-file fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Capture must finish before the host persists and acknowledges creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the automation catalog and use existing captured-bundle creation/parsing and garbage collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing catalog setAndFlush per successful non-idempotent create; bundle operations depend on capture misses, and existing garbage collection examines stored copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations ran for successful creates; no new persistence or cleanup scheduling is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Capture and persistence precede authoritative AutomationSet; garbage collection remains in the serialized mutation lifecycle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N selected/enabled customization references; U distinct URI keys not already granted on this connection, U <= N. Actual capture traffic depends on uncached bundle files/directories and their total bytes, not on all installed customizations or automation catalog entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new grant loop starts up to U asynchronous realpath operations without awaiting them or adding a limiter. Host catalog mutations are globally serialized by _mutationTail and capture iterates customization references sequentially. The client-filesystem provider limits content reads to 10; metadata/list operations are separate. No per-file concurrency increase is introduced by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing connection-wide ResourceSet deduplicates grants across automation actions, session actions, and session creation. Each new URI retains one grant and one realpath promise, including fallback to the lexical URI on failure. Host capture reuses a nonce-derived destination when present; references without a nonce receive a fresh destination. Providers without realpath capability perform no underlying realpath operation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced store dispatch, synchronous grant registration, production grant service, provider realpath, host capture cache, mutation sequencer, and content-read limiter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime timings or installed-plugin distribution are available. Cold grants can fan out by selected distinct customization roots, but the inspected path provides no evidence of a pathological count or unnecessary repeated boundary work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added per-new-URI grant work is required to enable the existing capture operation, is shared and deduplicated per connection, and is not synchronously awaited before dispatch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update an automation, including repeated saves, customization replacement, and updates without a session customization change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The store dispatches an update and waits for matching authoritative catalog state. The added branch runs only when changes.session.customizations is present. Existing host capture runs for session changes and precedes persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register and canonicalize newly encountered customization URI grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: U new realpath attempts, not N calls on every update. Zero on a warm same-URI save or update without customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automation updates added no grants of their own; grants created by existing session flows were already available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is synchronous; provider resolution is asynchronous and only awaited indirectly when access checks need it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing update dispatch and reverse-resource bundle capture for changed uncached customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatched action; no client resource traffic for unchanged captured references. Changed uncached bundles generate requests proportional to their entries and bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reuse comparisons, copy loop, network protocol, and read limiter applied before the diff; absent grants caused denial rather than a different optimized capture algorithm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required captures complete before catalog persistence and response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush the updated catalog and perform existing post-mutation captured-copy garbage collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing catalog flush per successful update, with unchanged cleanup behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful updates performed the same catalog persistence and cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence precedes the authoritative update; mutation completion retains the existing cleanup ordering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N submitted customization references; U previously unseen URI keys on the connection; K changed references requiring capture after comparing previous id/URI/nonce. Repeated edits to title, triggers, or other fields may resend a session template but do not imply U = N or K = N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Grant realpaths for U new URIs launch asynchronously. Existing updates are globally serialized on the host; capture processes references sequentially, with the shared provider's 10-content-read limiter for any copied bundles.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Repeated saves of identical URIs only parse/check N references and add no grants or grant realpath calls. Previously captured references with matching id, URI, and nonce are reused without contacting their client. Different nonce at the same URI does not create an additional client grant. Missing session/customizations adds no work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: verified both changed branches, ResourceSet deduplication, store session-template reuse, and host previous-reference comparisons.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of customizations and distinct URI replacements over a long connection is not measured. Retained grants scale with unique referenced roots, not number of saves, and are released on connection close.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Warm saves avoid new boundary work; no changed mechanism causes repeated copying, per-save grant accumulation for the same URI, or a new blocking await.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconnect with pending automation actions and close/dispose the connection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reconnect drains pending actions before queued outgoing messages. It deduplicates pending actions against queued clientSeq values, then re-runs the existing outgoing-grant hook for replayed actions. Terminal close clears URI keys and disposes grants.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Potential canonical-path resolution for replayed automation grants that are not already registered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero additional grant realpaths for warm URIs; at most one per distinct cold URI. Grant cleanup itself deletes in-memory entries rather than performing filesystem operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The outgoing-action hook was already called during replay but did not handle automation create/update actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No newly awaited filesystem operation in reconnect draining; later access checks can await grant promises.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Replay unacknowledged action notifications and flush the queued outbox.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing replay/outbox cardinality, with clientSeq deduplication; the diff adds no wire messages for permission grants.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical replay notifications and outbox ordering, without automation-specific grant registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing replay ordering is preserved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pending replayed actions and their customization references; grant allocation and realpath work depend on the union of previously ungranted URI keys, not the sum of references across every replay. Retention depends on unique granted URIs during the connection lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconnect constructs and sends replays in existing order, skipping sequences already queued. Any cold grant realpaths are asynchronous and can overlap; warm replays add none. No new replay notifications or reconnect loops are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ordinary soft reconnect retains the dedup set, so replayed same-URI grants are warm. Connection-setup restart explicitly clears grants; subsequent applicable grant registration is cold. Terminal close clears both the dedup set and grant store, and the resource service removes identity-owned grants. The grant store is also registered for disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: verified reconnect hook placement, queued-sequence deduplication, grant reset points, terminal-close cleanup, and registered disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Pending-action count and distinct URI turnover are not measured. No additional unbounded replay queue, resource watcher, or persistent grant lifecycle was introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable replay fan-out or retention regression. Grants reuse existing connection ownership and cleanup, and repeated references are deduplicated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across the complete two-file inventory and both full diffs. Traced added automation grant calls through production realpath boundaries, deduplication and cleanup, save callers, serialized host capture and persistence, capture reuse, reverse filesystem operations, base64 transport, and the shared read limiter. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bug or concrete performance-regression fix was established; the change repairs authorization for existing capture behavior.
